sites.rationale: ADAM10 has a single-pass type-I topology: signal peptide 1–19, extracellular 20–677, TM 678–698, intracellular 699–748. The C-terminus is cytoplasmic, leaving the mature N-terminus (residue 20, 658 residues from the TM boundary) as the only extracellular terminus; insert_after_residue=19 is the unique topology-derived junction. Residue_before=G (position 19, last SP residue) and residue_after=Q (position 20, first mature residue) were read directly from the numbered sequence. A critical caveat: ADAM10 carries a prodomain (approximately residues 20–211) that is cleaved by furin at the RKKR motif (residues 210–213) during maturation; a tag placed at position 19/20 sits within this prodomain and may be shed from the mature surface enzyme, making it unreliable as a stable surface label without a prodomain-cleavage-resistant design. Full-length HA-tagged ADAM10 expressed from pcDNA3.1 in mammalian cells; construct described as previously published (ref [49]). No residue or loop is named in the clip; position is derived from topology because the N-terminus (after SP cleavage at residue 19) is the sole extracellular terminus — the C-terminus (residues 699–748) is intracellular.

sources.claim: HA-tagged ADAM10 in the pcDNA3.1 vector was as described [ 49 ].

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It confirms a full-length HA-tagged ADAM10 construct but names no insertion residue, no loop, and reports no assay. The topology-derived rule places the tag at the sole extracellular terminus (after SP cleavage, insert_after_residue=19). Confidence is low because (1) no position is stated in the clip, (2) no functional or surface-expression assay is described, (3) the N-terminal region of the mature ectodomain is the prodomain, which is proteolytically removed by furin during normal ADAM10 maturation — a tag here may not persist on the mature cell-surface enzyme. No internal loop sites are supported by the ledger. The intracellular C-terminus (699–748) was considered and excluded as it is cytoplasmic.
